project.name: hello
project.summary: Staff draft and send push campaigns from a web dashboard. Background workers prepare the audience, deliver through Firebase Cloud Messaging, and record results that staff can review.

nodes.label: Staff dashboard
nodes.summary: Gives staff one place to sign in, manage their applications, and follow push campaigns.

nodes.label: Sign-in and navigation
nodes.summary: Opens the local staff session and routes staff to the selected application and screen.

nodes.label: Campaign workspace
nodes.summary: Lets staff compose, preview, send, or schedule a draft and watch its status.

nodes.label: Campaign results
nodes.summary: Shows campaign statistics, recorded delivery attempts, and read activity.

nodes.label: Audience and settings
nodes.summary: Shows app users, segments, templates, activity, and staff settings.

nodes.label: Staff and registry
nodes.summary: Lets authorized staff manage registry entries, grants, staff accounts, and onboarding.

nodes.label: Local Android Test Devices
nodes.summary: Downloads the standalone test APK, pairs Android phones over private HTTPS, and sends a campaign through the ordinary pipeline to one selected phone.

nodes.label: Shared screen components
nodes.summary: Provides common page controls, feedback, and display themes.

nodes.label: Browser request client
nodes.summary: Sends dashboard requests to the same-origin dashboard server and parses responses.

nodes.label: Dashboard server
nodes.summary: Serves the dashboard, keeps staff credentials server-side, and forwards allowed requests to the main server.

nodes.label: Request reference
nodes.summary: Shows how to call the main server and what responses to expect.

nodes.label: Main server
nodes.summary: Checks current access and handles campaign, audience, staff, and mobile requests.

nodes.label: Staff identity and access
nodes.summary: Signs staff in, manages their accounts, and checks current staff authority and application grants.

nodes.label: Application registry and grants
nodes.summary: Finds the apps a staff account can access and lets authorized staff manage registry records and grants.

nodes.label: Campaign drafts and history
nodes.summary: Stores drafts and templates and answers questions about campaign history, deliveries, and reads.

nodes.label: Send and schedule requests
nodes.summary: Validates send and schedule requests and records the durable work that the delivery system can act on.

nodes.label: Audience and segments
nodes.summary: Lists app users and devices and manages the segments that campaigns can target.

nodes.label: Mobile installations and receipts
nodes.summary: Manages mobile installation identity and records delivery or read observations from the app.

nodes.label: Application setup
nodes.summary: Handles scoped enrollment profiles, credential staging, and reviewed activation, cohort dry-run, and dispatch release requests.

nodes.label: Request and audit support
nodes.summary: Validates requests, returns consistent responses, and records staff actions.

nodes.label: Delivery pipeline
nodes.summary: Turns accepted campaigns into durable delivery work and records what happened during sending.

nodes.label: Scheduler and queued recovery
nodes.summary: Promotes due schedules, publishes send requests, recovers queued campaigns, and cleans up expired replay claims.

nodes.label: Audience preparation
nodes.summary: Checks the queued send, takes a snapshot of its audience, and creates delivery work for each eligible device.

nodes.label: Delivery worker
nodes.summary: Claims app-scoped delivery work, submits to the provider, and recovers interrupted work from stored state.

nodes.label: Delivery results and updates
nodes.summary: Records attempt evidence, finalizes campaigns, and publishes delivery updates for downstream consumers.

nodes.label: Provider and queue connections
nodes.summary: Connects the workers to Kafka and Firebase Cloud Messaging using scoped configuration.

nodes.label: Worker runtime and replay
nodes.summary: Starts the configured worker mode and supports approved reprocessing of send records.

nodes.label: Data definitions and access
nodes.summary: Defines how PostgreSQL stores business records and how the services read and update them.

nodes.label: Storage changes
nodes.summary: Applies changes to how campaigns, identities, permissions, and delivery work are stored.

nodes.label: Database queries
nodes.summary: Defines the named SQL operations used by the main server and background jobs.

nodes.label: Database connections and repositories
nodes.summary: Opens PostgreSQL connections and adapts queries for callers that use repository interfaces.

nodes.label: Setup and operations
nodes.summary: Sets up, releases, verifies, and maintains the server and its background processes.

nodes.label: Credential staging and verification
nodes.summary: Stages reserved Firebase credentials through a private connection and verifies OAuth access for the selected application.

nodes.label: Bootstrap, replay, and retention
nodes.summary: Creates the first super-admin and provides restricted commands for reprocessing and retention.

nodes.label: Build and release
nodes.summary: Builds services and defines runtime policies, database and broker settings, and local stack composition.

nodes.label: Service health and signals
nodes.summary: Reports worker progress, backlog, provider outcomes, and health for operators.

nodes.label: Development and verification tools
nodes.summary: Runs local workflows, verifies contracts, and provides fixtures for dependencies in development.

nodes.label: Automated tests
nodes.summary: Checks feature behavior and exercises the dashboard, storage, broker, and delivery boundaries.

nodes.label: Environment boundaries and release gates
nodes.summary: Keeps the ./dev stack isolated from shared staging and production. Staging has recorded single-device Android smoke and receipt results, but end-to-end acceptance remains open; production dispatch is on hold pending target evidence and release approval.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.summary: Stores campaign state, permissions, audiences, delivery attempts, receipts, and pending publications.

nodes.label: Kafka
nodes.summary: Carries accepted send requests to admission and delivery updates to downstream consumers.

nodes.label: Firebase Cloud Messaging
nodes.summary: Receives push requests from the delivery worker and handles transport to mobile devices.

nodes.label: Mobile apps
nodes.summary: Register installations, receive push notifications, and can report receipt or read activity.

edges.label: Send or schedule a campaign
edges.description: The campaign page builds a same-origin dashboard URL at runtime and sends the staff action with its current CSRF token.

edges.label: Dashboard requests
edges.description: The shared client sends browser requests under /bff for the dashboard session or allowlisted application data.

edges.label: Forward permitted API requests
edges.description: The dashboard server calls the configured API and holds the API key and staff tokens on the server.

edges.label: Forward send and schedule requests
edges.description: The dashboard forwards app-scoped send and schedule actions to the matching main server handlers.

edges.label: Load campaign reporting
edges.description: The results screen requests stored statistics, delivery attempts, and reads through the dashboard server.

edges.label: Read campaign reporting
edges.description: The dashboard forwards allowed campaign reporting requests to the main server.

edges.label: Commit a schedule or send request
edges.description: A send transaction stores the campaign, acceptance data, audit record, and send outbox entry together.

edges.label: Read and write application records
edges.description: The API uses its own database connection pool for staff, campaign, application, and mobile requests.

edges.label: Find due schedules and pending work
edges.description: Independent scheduler tasks read due schedules, unsent outbox rows, and recoverable queued campaigns.

edges.label: Publish a send request
edges.description: The scheduler publishes a committed send request to its configured Kafka stream.

edges.label: Consume a send request
edges.description: The admission worker validates the event source and processes each accepted send at its checkpoint.

edges.label: Recover an eligible queued campaign
edges.description: Scheduler recovery invokes the same preparer used by admission and can prepare the campaign before Kafka consumption.

edges.label: Store audience and device work
edges.description: Preparation writes the audience snapshot and eligible device work as durable database records.

edges.label: Poll app-scoped delivery work
edges.description: Delivery discovers and claims actionable work for its configured application from PostgreSQL.

edges.label: Submit an authorized push
edges.description: The delivery path calls the provider after claiming the attempt and rechecking its authority.

edges.label: Record delivery evidence
edges.description: The worker persists provider attempt evidence and checks that the result belongs to the current attempt.

edges.label: Publish delivery updates
edges.description: The delivery worker publishes versioned updates for downstream consumers on a separate stream.

edges.label: Transport push notification
edges.description: Firebase Cloud Messaging handles transport to the target mobile installation.

edges.label: Manage a mobile installation
edges.description: The optional mobile API supports registration, refresh, logout, account switch, and state queries.

edges.label: Report receipt or read activity
edges.description: The mobile app may submit a capability-authorized observation for an installation and campaign.

edges.label: Store a mobile observation
edges.description: The API records accepted observations alongside delivery data for later reporting.

edges.label: Read campaign statistics
edges.description: The results endpoint reads the latest campaign statistics from stored data.

edges.label: Request reserved credential staging
edges.description: The optional setup service calls the configured provisioner over mutually authenticated TLS.

edges.label: Claim and record verification work
edges.description: The control plane uses app-scoped verification jobs and accepts completion only from the current owner.

edges.label: Create the first super-admin
edges.description: The one-shot command uses the SUPER_ADMIN role already seeded by the schema.

edges.label: Manage local test devices
edges.description: The loopback dashboard proxies authenticated device actions and sends to the local helper.

edges.label: Issue one-use pairing QR
edges.description: The helper fetches a fresh QR on an owner-only Unix socket. Android uses the separate mobile HTTPS listener.

edges.label: Create and send a test campaign
edges.description: The helper reuses the signed-in BFF session and ordinary application campaign routes.

annotations.note: The acceptance transaction commits campaign state and its send outbox entry together. An authorized retry with the retained key returns the existing acceptance.
The outbox publisher and queued recovery run independently. Recovery and Kafka admission share one audience preparer.
A provider call and a database write happen separately. Persist the original attempt evidence if the provider outcome is uncertain.

flows.title: Send a campaign
flows.description: Follow a staff member's send request from the campaign page to Firebase Cloud Messaging.

steps.note: Staff confirm Send on a draft. The page passes the same request key if this send is retried.
The dashboard server checks the session and forwards the allowed request.
The API checks application access and commits the campaign as QUEUED with a pending send message.
PostgreSQL keeps the campaign and its pending send message even if the broker is unavailable.
The scheduler publishes the stored send request to Kafka.
Kafka carries the request to the admission worker.
Admission verifies the source and resolves the campaign audience.
The saved audience snapshot and device work are ready for the delivery worker.
Delivery polls PostgreSQL, claims eligible device attempts, and submits them to Firebase.
Firebase handles transport to the target mobile installation.

flows.title: Schedule a send and recover queued work
flows.description: See how the scheduler prepares a due campaign even when Kafka admission has yet to run.

steps.note: Staff choose a future send time on the campaign page.
The dashboard server forwards the permitted schedule request.
The API validates the schedule and saves it with the campaign.
The stored schedule gives the scheduler a durable record to revisit when it becomes due.
Promotion queues the due campaign. The independent recovery task can find the queued campaign and prepare it from the database.
The shared preparer resolves the audience and stores the delivery work once.
The delivery worker can pick up the saved device work on a later poll.

flows.title: Track a push and its receipt
flows.description: See where provider results and mobile observations originate and how they reach campaign reporting.

steps.note: The delivery worker submits a scoped attempt and receives evidence about the provider outcome.
Firebase may transport the push to the target installation after accepting the request.
The app may send an observation of receipt or a read action.
The receipt endpoint checks the capability and records the observation.
PostgreSQL stores the mobile observation alongside the separate evidence recorded by the delivery worker.
The campaign reporting endpoints read recorded attempts and mobile activity from PostgreSQL.
The dashboard server returns the allowed reporting response.
Staff can inspect delivery attempts and reads while reviewing a campaign.

flows.title: Pair an Android phone and send a test push
flows.description: The isolated real-FCM profile enrolls test phones on private Wi-Fi and directs each test campaign to one selected installation.

steps.note: Open the dashboard link printed by ./dev up --real-fcm and download the standalone test APK.
Create a one-use pairing QR for each phone. The helper requests the QR over its private Unix socket.
Scanning the QR opens a short-lived mobile session and enrolls the installation over private HTTPS.
Select one enrolled phone and submit a test push using the normal dashboard and API path.
The worker submits the claimed delivery to the configured Firebase test project.

tour.title: Start where staff work
tour.note: The dashboard is where staff draft a campaign, choose an audience, and review the outcome.

tour.title: Check who can do what
tour.note: The API checks current staff authority and application grants before changing a campaign.

tour.title: Keep a durable record
tour.note: PostgreSQL holds the campaign, who it targets, and work that still needs to run.

tour.title: Prepare and send in the background
tour.note: The scheduler hands off pending work, admission prepares the audience, and the delivery worker calls Firebase.

tour.title: Open the campaign screen
tour.note: This is where staff send or schedule a draft and follow its progress.

tour.title: Trace the environment boundaries
tour.note: The simulator, local real-FCM profile, staging pilot, and production readiness gates have separate state and evidence.
